title: Severe hyperkalaemia
stem: Resus 1. A 68-year-old man on haemodialysis missed his last two sessions. He feels weak and dizzy. HR 44, BP 88/52, RR 20, SpO2 95%, GCS 15. The nurse hands you his ECG.

events.say: The monitor slows: HR 32, BP 72/40. He is grey and drowsy.
events.untreated: His bradycardia worsened and calcium was never given.

review.text: Glucose infusion. UKKA 2023: if the pre-treatment glucose is under 7 mmol/L, follow insulin–glucose with 10% glucose at 50 mL/h for 5 hours. His glucose is 6.2, so the script now includes it; the old station did not.

Hospital Authority hyperkalaemia guidance was not available to check; the doses are UKKA 2023 (calcium gluconate 10% 30 mL; insulin 10 units with 25 g glucose; salbutamol 10–20 mg). Atropine dose depends on the algorithm (AHA 1 mg; RCUK 500 micrograms).

notes:
Checked against the UK Kidney Association clinical practice guideline 'Treatment of acute hyperkalaemia in adults' (2023) and RCUK 2025 special circumstances.

Three steps: protect the heart, shift potassium into cells, remove potassium, and monitor.
• Protect: IV calcium if there are ECG changes — calcium gluconate 10% 30 mL or calcium chloride 10% 10 mL over 5–10 minutes; repeat if the ECG does not improve within 5–10 minutes. It works in minutes and lasts 30–60 minutes; it does not lower potassium.
• Shift: insulin 10 units soluble insulin with 25 g glucose (e.g. 50 mL of 50% or 250 mL of 10%) over 15 minutes; if glucose is under 7 mmol/L before treatment, follow with 10% glucose 50 mL/h for 5 hours; check glucose at 0, 15, 30, 60, 90, 120, 180, 240, 300 and 360 minutes (hypoglycaemia risk, especially in renal failure). Salbutamol 10–20 mg nebulised as an adjunct (not alone).
• Remove: dialysis for severe hyperkalaemia in renal failure; potassium binders (sodium zirconium cyclosilicate 10 g three times daily, or patiromer).
• Sodium bicarbonate is not routine; consider only with metabolic acidosis (and specialist advice in dialysis patients).

Your notes on pacing cover hyperkalaemia in bradycardia (calcium gluconate after the potassium result); this station follows UKKA 2023 in full.

Perfect script checked against a UKKA 2023 checklist, an AHA bradycardia checklist, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Added: the plan named (protect, shift, remove, monitor), the glucose infusion for a pre-treatment glucose under 7, atropine and pacing if the bradycardia persists, potassium sources stopped, the cause and admission.

Shift the potassium: insulin 10 units of soluble insulin with 25 g glucose IV over 15 minutes. His glucose is 6.2, under 7, so a glucose infusion follows: 10% at 50 mL an hour for 5 hours. And salbutamol 10 to 20 mg nebulised as an adjunct.

Pacing pads on now; if he stays bradycardic and hypotensive, atropine and then transcutaneous pacing.
